brief: Newsquawk previews the US September 2026 jobs report, due Oct 2 at 08:30 EDT. Consensus sees +98K nonfarm payrolls after August's +162K, which analysts say may have been flattered by favourable seasonal adjustments and could be revised down, with that revision raising upside risk to the September print even as a correction lower is possible; Barclays separately argues its claims-based models overstate the likely gain and that minimal revisions would put September below 50K. Unemployment is seen flat at 4.1%, matching the Chicago Fed's real-time forecast and the FOMC's own lowered end-2026 projection (4.1%, from 4.3%). Average hourly earnings are expected at +0.3% M/M, +3.2% Y/Y. Labour proxies mostly point to strength: claims fell, ADP beat (+90K), Revelio and Challenger (fewest September job cuts since 2022) improved, and PMI/ISM surveys show hiring at multi-year highs, though staffing is harder to find. Consumer confidence diverges, with job-availability perceptions and six-month job expectations both weakening. Fed officials call the labour market stable and near full employment, keeping focus on inflation, and several still flag a possible further hike, even as money-market pricing for an October hike has fallen to ~34% from ~70% after a soft August PCE print.
